All five functions are implemented in `problems.py` and pass my checks, including every docstring example and the called-out edge cases:

- **`parse_duration`** — anchored regex `(?:(\d+)h)?(?:(\d+)m)?(?:(\d+)s)?` with `fullmatch`, plus an at-least-one-component check. This structurally rejects out-of-order components, duplicate/unknown units, bare units, negatives, whitespace, and trailing garbage (all → `ValueError`).
- **`luhn_valid`** — strips spaces/hyphens, returns `False` (never raises) on empty or non-digit input, then the standard double-every-second-digit-from-the-right checksum.
- **`flatten`** — recursive walk joining keys with `sep`; empty nested dicts contribute nothing, lists and other non-dict values pass through, input is never mutated.
- **`top_k_frequent`** — `Counter` + sort by `(-count, word)`; `k <= 0` → `[]`, oversized `k` returns all distinct words.
- **`rolling_max`** — monotonic deque of indices (O(n)); verified against a brute-force `max()` reference on 200k elements in well under the time budget. `window <= 0` → `ValueError`, `window > len(nums)` → `[]`.

No new modules, no signature or docstring changes, no commits.
